Prepared by: PMA Partner  |  Confidential Working Draft — July 2026

1. Executive Summary

The recommended approach for Assist34 is to shift from a "generic outsourcing" narrative to the position of a specialist partner that delivers accuracy, speed, and continuity of operational capacity for travel operations. August should be used to engage procurement and operations teams ahead of their autumn/year-end capacity planning.

365-Day GoalAugust OutputSuccess Signal
Demand creation4 organic LinkedIn posts + 2 long-form assets + ad setsCompany profile visits and form completions
Demand captureA single "Operational Readiness Check" offer pageMQL; corporate email + suitable sector/role
Sales handoff48-hour response standard and CRM follow-up flowMeeting rate, pipeline value

Recommended Decision

Launch the August media investment at €1,000: 60% Google Search, 40% LinkedIn. This balances search intent with target-account reach.

Package the offer as a "free operational capacity / data accuracy assessment" — more concrete than a generic "contact us" call, and more qualified for the sales team.

Shift content away from recruitment and corporate-celebration density toward proof, working method, expertise, and customer operational benefit.

Note: The budget and performance ranges below are planning assumptions; they should be recalibrated using real CPL, conversion, and sales-quality data from the first 30 days.

2. Current State & Positioning

Assist34 provides 24/7, tailored business support services for travel companies, retailers, and airlines. The service portfolio covers hotel contract and rate data, reservations, inventory/sales, content-data management, aviation, and IT support.

Strength / Gap & Risk / Marketing Response

StrengthGap / RiskMarketing Response
Vertical expertise: tourism operations, contracting, reservations, and rate management.The value proposition is broad; without buyer-specific packaging it risks being perceived as "generic BPO".3 solution packages: Contract & Content Ops / Reservation & CX / Data & Revenue Support.
24/7 and multilingual operations potential.Recent social visibility skews toward recruitment, team, and celebration themes.At least 2 expertise/proof posts and 1 lead magnet every month.
Touchpoints across the Europe–MENA tourism ecosystem.Limited visibility into case studies, SLAs, and process proof.Anonymized before/after process examples, checklists, and expert commentary.
"Assist34 is the specialist outsourcing partner that keeps travel brands' critical operations accurate, up to date, and scalable — 24/7."

Recommended Offer Structure

1

Entry Offer

30-minute "Operational Readiness Check" — 3 bottlenecks, 1 priority matrix, a starting approach.

2

Conversion Asset

"Peak-Season Operations Checklist: Contracts, Rates, Inventory & Reservations" (downloadable PDF/landing page).

3

Sales Offer

A 4-week pilot / controlled transition package — a one-pager clarifying scope, SLA, reporting, and responsibilities.

Language & tone: Primary language should be English; select content can be adapted into Turkish or Arabic depending on target account and market mix. Tone: clear, technical but accessible — process proof, case studies, business impact, and expert opinion instead of "we are the best". Free Analysis PDFs.

4. Competitive / Category Landscape

Category scanning shows that B2B transportation and travel-operations players emphasize technology, operational proof, and enterprise segments. While not offering the exact same service set, these players set the buyer's messaging standard as category benchmarks.

Observed ApproachImplication for Assist34
Emphasizes the combination of software + operations; a content, case-study, webinar, and lead-generation approach.Position the service not just as a "team" but as a measurable operational outcome.
Uses technology, a professional operations network, punctual service, and multilingual content.Visualize the proof: process flow, control mechanisms, team expertise, platform/integration.
Clearly packages enterprise partner segments (agencies, hotels, holdings) and a 24/7, multilingual service.Explicitly name the target-account segment in landing pages and ads; avoid generic targeting.
Frames staff transportation around operational efficiency, route planning, and digital management.Translate service headlines into business outcomes: accuracy, speed, risk reduction, revenue protection.

6. Google Ads Plan

Goal: capture people actively searching for a solution. In the first month, Google Search should focus only on high-intent search terms and brand defense; Display/Performance Max should not be activated until sufficient conversion data exists.

Implementation Notes

  • Negative keywords from the start: jobs, salary, course, free, consumer booking, transfer, hotel reservation customer service. Run weekly search-term cleanups.
  • Landing page requirements: target sector, process/output, 3 proof elements, short form, calendar alternative, privacy note.

Sample Ad Copy

Headline: "Travel Operations Outsourcing | 24/7 Specialist Support"

Description: "Keep contracts, rates, inventory and reservations accurate at peak demand. Tailored travel operations support for tour operators, OTAs and airlines. Book a readiness check."

First 5 Actions

  • Build 1 solution landing page on the website, focused on sector and business outcome; link it visibly from the homepage.
  • Align the first target-account list of 100–300 companies with sales; tier by country, segment, and contact function. Mailing can be done.
  • Design the "Peak-Season Operations Checklist" asset and a one-page readiness-check offer.
  • Verify Google/LinkedIn tags, UTM standards, and CRM feedback before ads go live.
  • Set up a weekly 30-minute marketing–sales growth rhythm; rejected-lead reasons matter as much as budget.
  • Social media designs should be started.
